caveat: Compiled from domain knowledge and not checked against an official government concordance. Section numbers are machine-verified to exist in the extracted statute text; the correctness of each pairing is not.

entries.note: Waging war against Government of India.
Sedition repealed. BNS 152 (act endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity) is NOT a renumbering -- different elements and scope.
Disobedience to order of public servant.
Negligent act likely to spread infection.
Rash driving on a public way.
Culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
Death by negligence. BNS 106(2) adds a distinct, heavier offence for fleeing without reporting -- no IPC predecessor.
Abetment of suicide of child/insane person.
Attempt to suicide not re-enacted as a general offence; BNS 226 covers only attempt to suicide to compel/restrain a public servant.
Causing death of a quick unborn child.
Grievous hurt to deter public servant.
Act endangering life or personal safety.
Kidnapping/abducting a woman to compel marriage.
Importation of a girl from a foreign country.
Sexual intercourse by husband on separation.
Sexual intercourse by a person in authority.
IPC 376DA (gang rape of a woman under 16) and 376DB (under 12) are merged into BNS 70(2).
No counterpart in the BNS. Non-consensual acts against men and transgender persons are consequently not covered by a general provision.
IPC 397 and 398 both map onto BNS 311.
Punishment for criminal breach of trust.
Breach of trust by public servant/banker.
Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property.
Forgery for the purpose of cheating.
Using a forged document as genuine.
Adultery; already struck down in Joseph Shine v. Union of India (2018) and not re-enacted.
Cruelty by husband or relatives. BNS 85 carries the offence; the definition in the IPC Explanation becomes a standalone BNS 86.
Intentional insult to provoke breach of peace.
IPC 506 Part I -> BNS 351(2); Part II (threat to cause death/grievous hurt) -> BNS 351(3). Case data citing '506(II)' maps to 351(3).
Word or gesture insulting a woman's modesty.
Punishment for attempting to commit offences.
When police may arrest without warrant.
Right to meet an advocate during interrogation.
Arrest, how made. BNSS 43(3) newly permits use of handcuffs in specified cases.
Right to be informed of grounds of arrest.
Person arrested not to be detained over 24 hours.
FIR. BNSS 173 newly permits registration irrespective of territorial jurisdiction (Zero FIR) and electronic filing.
Detention beyond 24 hours. The 15-day police custody period may now be sought in parts across the first 40/60 days.
Police report on completion of investigation.
Magisterial inquiry into a death in custody.
Prosecution of judges and public servants.
Supply of copies to the accused.
Release on probation of good conduct.
Maximum period of detention. BNSS 479 adds release on bond after one-third of the maximum sentence for a first-time offender, and bars the benefit for offences punishable with life.
Special powers of High Court/Sessions Court.
Bar to taking cognizance after limitation.
Saving of inherent powers of the High Court.
Evidence may be given of facts in issue.
The proviso on discovery of facts sits inside BSA 23(2).
Opinion of the Examiner of Electronic Evidence.
IEA 65A/65B are consolidated into BSA 63, which materially expands the certificate requirement for electronic records.
Presumption as to abetment of suicide.
Court may presume existence of facts.
Presumption as to absence of consent in rape.
Sexual intercourse by employing deceitful means or a false promise of marriage.
Murder by a group of five or more on grounds of race, caste, community, sex, birthplace, language or personal belief (mob lynching).
Causing death by rash/negligent driving and fleeing without reporting to police or magistrate.
Terrorist act (previously reachable only under the UAPA).
Act endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India (occupies the space vacated by sedition, with different elements).
Audio-video recording of search and seizure.
Trial in absentia of a proclaimed offender.
Trial, inquiry and proceedings in electronic mode.
